source-integrity.provenance: Q3 SEC/issuer results and September Amazon collaboration are primary; issuer IR market quote is used only for current valuation context
source-integrity.freshness: Q3 results 2026-07-29; Amazon collaboration 2026-09-08; IR quote current in September 2026
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: Amazon collaboration is issuer-announced and not counted as independent corroboration; operating claims remain primary-source grounded

thesisQuality.basis: Leadership in low-power compute/connectivity plus automotive, IoT and new data-center programs supports durable differentiation, while handset and custom-silicon substitution risks remain.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q3 revenue fell 4% and non-GAAP EPS fell 20% year over year, while automotive+IoT revenue grew 28% and management expects faster non-handset growth.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Current IR quote around $161 combined with diversified FY29 targets offers plausible upside, but those targets require substantial execution and are not treated as achieved.

catalystScore.basis: Multi-generation Amazon AI-data-center collaboration, data-center ramp, automotive pipeline and broader edge-AI roadmap are multiple material identifiable catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Management has articulated measurable diversification targets and completed Modular acquisition while maintaining capital returns; execution against new targets remains prospective.

alignment2036.basis: AI compute, low-power processing, connectivity, automotive, industrial/robotics and data-center infrastructure are foundational across multiple plausible 2036 technology futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Common compute/connectivity/IP capabilities span handsets, automotive, IoT, robotics, PCs and data centers.

bottleneckControl.basis: Wireless/connectivity IP, power-efficient compute and advanced optical/custom silicon participate in high-value qualification and infrastructure constraints.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Diversification across edge and cloud creates multiple paths, but handset concentration and dependence on successful data-center entry remain material.

substitutionResilience.basis: Patent/IP, connectivity and system-level integration create barriers, offset by customer in-house silicon and competing architectures.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Q3 explicitly cited challenging memory and supply conditions; fabless diversification helps but external semiconductor/memory dependencies remain meaningful.

pricingPower.basis: Licensing/IP economics and differentiated premium silicon support value capture, though current earnings pressure prevents an exceptional score.

riskEvidence.basis: Handset concentration, memory/supply constraints, customer in-house silicon and unproven data-center economics can offset diversification upside.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC results, issuer operating data, a September named-customer collaboration and current market quote cover core thesis/catalysts; segment incremental margins and data-center economics remain unproven.

scoreRecord.thesis: Qualcomm can reuse differentiated low-power compute, connectivity and IP across edge, automotive, robotics and data-center markets, creating a credible diversification path beyond handsets.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Customer in-house silicon, supply constraints and failure to convert ambitious data-center/automotive targets into profitable revenue could leave handset concentration dominant.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Initial revenue evidence from the Amazon/custom-silicon data-center collaboration and acceleration of non-handset revenue into FY27.
